The Jacobian of x=q^u,y=q^(1-u)w is q log(1/q); J(q)=int_0^q -log(t)/(1-t²) dt normalizes the density, with J(q)=q(log(1/q)+1)+O(q³log(1/q)). Almost-everywhere density convergence, unit total mass and Scheffe give TV. Hyperbolic sinh(d/2)=sinh R sin(a/2) yields two complementary positive-part limiting side-length ratios; max |1-2U| is Unif(0,1). Independently checked density normalization and mark split numerically for q=.01 and .0001; tests corroborate, not prove continuum result.
